reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the raw EventDefinition StructureDefinition report, the direct SearchParameters finding whose affectedResources include EventDefinition, and the shared Resource/DomainResource behavior context. I treated shared Resource and DomainResource behavior as context only because EventDefinition is neither base resource. I used the deterministic aggregate only after forming the resource-level judgment.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 EventDefinition is trial-use/FMM 0, so ordinary compatibility expectations are weak. That lowers the burden for proportionate cleanup, but it does not erase targeted concerns where a same-named field silently changes governance meaning or where conformance metadata can be preserved with low-cost aliases.

overall.oneLineConclusion: EventDefinition keeps its R4 identity and is mostly shape-compatible; migration is local and targeted, so avoidable semantic and conformance breaks still deserve per-change preservation review.

reasoning.thesisMd: EventDefinition is not a resource-level redesign. The R6 StructureDefinition keeps the same canonical resource identity, DomainResource base, local element set except for optional additions, and common local cardinalities. R4 instances generally remain structurally representable in R6. The material migration work is concentrated in same-name semantic changes, one primitive-type/codegen change, an extensible binding change, warning-level constraints, and a direct SearchParameter canonical identity consolidation.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The actual migration shape is mostly stable with local breaks. There are no local removals, no cardinality tightening, no reference target removals, no new mandatory elements, and no modifier flag changes. `EventDefinition.usage` changes primitive identity from `string` to `markdown`, which matters for generated APIs and type-aware tooling but is usually string-compatible on the wire. `EventDefinition.subject[x]` keeps the same CodeableConcept/Reference(Group) shape but changes an extensible binding. `EventDefinition.jurisdiction` is the largest resource-specific concern because the same path changes from jurisdiction of intended use to jurisdiction of the maintaining authority, with migration to `useContext` requiring policy judgment.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a broad resource migration program is not already unavoidable, compatibility leverage remains high on a per-change basis. Low R4 maturity means not every cleanup needs preservation, but the aggregate should not be used to dismiss low-cost compatibility designs. Preserving old semantics where feasible, adding transition aliases, or documenting precise migration rules can materially reduce risk for implementers without carrying an entire obsolete EventDefinition model.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking alternative is for `jurisdiction`: preserve the R4 intended-use meaning and add a clearly named maintainer-authority jurisdiction slot, or provide an explicit transition that avoids silent reinterpretation. The direct SearchParameter break also has a plausible low-cost alternative: keep old per-resource canonical SearchParameter definitions as deprecated aliases to the R6 multi-base definitions. The `usage` and `subject[x]` alternatives are only partial because preserving old type/binding choices would reduce R6 computability or create duplicate representations. Optional additions such as `versionAlgorithm[x]` and `copyrightLabel` do not need less-breaking R4-to-R6 designs.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct behavior finding is real but not an EventDefinition instance migration driver. Search query codes for EventDefinition usually remain available, but canonical SearchParameter URLs move from per-resource definitions to CanonicalResource/MetadataResource definitions. That can break CapabilityStatement comparison, generated clients, conformance tests, and registries that key by canonical URL. Shared Resource and DomainResource operation or HTTP behavior findings are important ecosystem context but are not scored as EventDefinition-specific resource changes.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: I agree with the deterministic aggregate's main result: `majorMigrationAlreadyUnavoidable` should be `No`, the migration shape is mostly stable with local breaks, and the compatibility posture should be `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The independent review puts extra emphasis on keeping the direct SearchParameter conformance break separate from EventDefinition instance migration, and on treating `jurisdiction` as the one resource-specific standards-review-worthy change despite the low FMM baseline.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural shape because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were present and the raw report identifies no identity break, removals, or cardinality tightening. Prevalence confidence is lower because no representative EventDefinition instance corpus or official ballot rationale was supplied, and the R6 jurisdiction ValueSet target is external to the supplied core package.

findingConsiderations.title: EventDefinition.jurisdiction changes from intended jurisdiction of use to maintaining authority jurisdiction
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main EventDefinition-specific Revisit item. The wire shape remains valid, but the same path now answers a different governance question. Existing values may need expert migration to `useContext`, maintainer jurisdiction, or both, and a low-cost model alternative could avoid silent reinterpretation.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the only direct behavior finding for EventDefinition. It does not usually remove the query code, but it changes conformance identity for search parameters. Deprecated per-resource aliases would preserve CapabilityStatement and generator compatibility at relatively low cost, so this remains an avoidable compatibility concern even though it is not an instance migration program.

findingConsiderations.title: EventDefinition.usage changes primitive type from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a targeted generated-model and validator migration chore rather than a broad data transform. Existing JSON values are still string-shaped, but primitive-specific APIs, schemas, and FHIRPath type checks can change. The R6 markdown goal is reasonable, so preservation value is moderate rather than decisive.

findingConsiderations.title: EventDefinition.subject[x] CodeableConcept binding changes from subject-type to participant-resource-types
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The extensible binding change can affect authoring, indexing, and warning-as-error validation for a field tied to event applicability. Because the binding is extensible and the choice shape is unchanged, it is a local terminology migration rather than evidence that EventDefinition needs broad redesign migration.

findingConsiderations.title: EventDefinition.experimental has stronger R6 lifecycle meaning
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This can alter publication filters or lifecycle promotion rules, but it is still a same-boolean semantic tightening. Given FMM 0 and a coherent R6 goal of marking content that should never be used genuinely, it is best handled as migration guidance rather than as a standards blocker.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional EventDefinition.versionAlgorithm[x]
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This optional addition is reverse-direction loss for R6-to-R4 downgrade, not an R4-to-R6 instance break. It may need downgrade policy when populated, but it does not contribute to major migration unavoidability for R4 EventDefinition instances.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional EventDefinition.copyrightLabel
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is optional display/legal metadata. It has no R4-to-R6 acceptance impact and only creates a native-slot gap when downgrading R6 content to R4.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 strengthens warning-level canonical name and URL constraints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The constraints are warning severity, so base validation should not reject R4 instances. Warning-as-error pipelines may need policy updates, but this is not a hard or resource-level migration driver.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This affects generic discovery and operation advertisement behavior, but it is shared Resource/DomainResource context rather than an EventDefinition-specific behavior finding. It should inform ecosystem migration planning without changing the EventDefinition resource-level conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 core removes the Resource $meta operation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generic Resource operation removals can matter to clients managing metadata on any resource, including EventDefinition instances, but under the review scope they remain shared base behavior context and are not counted as direct EventDefinition resource redesign.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit `EventDefinition.jurisdiction` and the shared canonical-resource jurisdiction pattern to avoid silent reinterpretation. Either preserve the R4 intended-use meaning, add a named maintainer-authority jurisdiction element, or publish explicit migration rules for when old values move to `useContext`.

For EventDefinition search conformance, consider publishing deprecated per-resource SearchParameter canonical aliases or clear equivalence guidance so CapabilityStatement comparison and generated clients do not fail solely on canonical URL changes.
Document local migration chores for `usage` string-to-markdown APIs, `subject[x]` terminology recoding, `experimental` lifecycle interpretation, and R6-only optional metadata downgrade policy.

caveats: No representative corpus of R4 EventDefinition instances was supplied, so prevalence and business impact are inferred from element purpose.
No official R4-to-R6 ballot rationale was supplied for the semantic changes, so proportionality judgments are based on computable definitions and report evidence.
The R6 jurisdiction ValueSet target is external to the supplied R6 core package, limiting terminology-specific confidence for that binding.
Shared Resource and DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, per the resource-review instructions.
